conviction_note: Georgia, about 95% of earnings, looks strong on NBG standalone data (9M GEL 1.06bn, +18%, snippet only). That is probably tracked and partly priced after Lion Finance's beat lifted the stock 4.9% over 4-5 Nov. Against it, TBC Bank Uzbekistan's own statutory statements show a Q3 loss of 357.7bn soum (about GEL 80m), provisions up about 70% on the H1 quarterly run-rate, NPLs from 10.4% to 13.4% and a 9% QoQ loan shrink in soum, all against management's H2-growth message. findings.finding: TBC Bank Uzbekistan's own statutory statements show a 3Q26 net loss of 357.7bn soum (about GEL 80m, about USD 30m at 11,903 UZS/USD). H1 was a profit of 288.1bn. Implied Q3 provisions are about 556bn soum (9M 1.2tn less H1 643.9bn) against about 322bn a quarter in H1. NPLs rose from 10.4% to 13.4%, the loan book fell from 8.5tn to 7.7tn soum (-9% QoQ) and income from about 1.5tn to about 1.2tn a quarter. The August release had said the loan book 'has stabilised and is starting to return to growth'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Uzbek line has been punished. 3Q25 (6 Nov 2025): -11.87% on the day, with analysts pressing on Uzbek risk weights and costs. 1Q26 (6 May 2026): -4.17% on the Uzbek 'recalibration'. 2Q26, when the release said Uzbekistan had stabilised: +0.66%.
findings.why_not_priced: Published at 22:50 Tashkent on 30 Oct, after the London close, in Uzbek local press, in soum and on local GAAP; I found no London coverage of it. TBCG then rose 2.25%, 3.58% and 1.29% on 3-5 Nov with the Georgian peer, and its 5-day run-up is only -1.25%, so the price is not visibly holding an Uzbek loss. Caveats that shrink it: local GAAP has diverged from IFRS before (3Q25 local loss of 70.7bn soum while IFRS Uzbekistan earned GEL 41.1m; H1 2026 local beat IFRS), the soum statements cover the bank and not Payme/BILLZ, and the unexplained -8.9% on 30 Oct (Georgian peers -4 to -5%) may already carry part of it. Net of the rest of the company: Uzbekistan was about 5% of group profit in 2Q, so even a GEL 40-60m swing is 10-15% of the quarter, and Georgia's strength (separate finding) offsets part of it.
findings.independence: The same statutory series, read in H1, links the IFRS and local NPLs: local 10.4% at 1 July against IFRS 10.6% at 30 June, so the local Q3 NPL of 13.4% probably carries into IFRS. https://www.uzdaily.uz/en/tbc-bank-reports-185-rise-in-first-half-net-profit/ (21 Jul 2026). No source outside this series points the same way.

findings.finding: NBG standalone data, as reported in the Georgian press, put TBC Bank (Georgia) at a 9M 2026 profit of GEL 1.06bn, +18% YoY. Against the H1 standalone GEL 683.9m on the NBG table, that implies about GEL 376m for 3Q against about 354m in 2Q, so Georgia (95% of group earnings) probably prints about GEL 400m on IFRS, around +15% YoY.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Georgian strength alone has not lifted the stock on a results day when Uzbekistan disappointed: 3Q25 Georgia grew and the stock fell 11.9%. On FY25 with new targets (20 Feb 2026) it rose 8.5%.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is -0.11 (run-up only, no anchor) and the 20-day run-up +2.1%. My negative lean agrees weakly with the lean, but it rests on Uzbek local-GAAP data the run-up does not reflect, offset by Georgian strength the peer rally has largely priced.
language_note: The domestic UK sources (the RNS on Investegate) carried the date, the 07:00 GMT timestamp, the PDMR and the TR-1, all of which the international wires also carry. The load-bearing evidence came from local press in Uzbekistan (UzDaily) and Georgia (bm.ge, gbc.ge), which neither the UK domestic nor the international English sources carried. So the UK domestic half added nothing the English sources did not already carry.
lessons_applied: 'You were right about the number and too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 6.5 to 7.0, the base rate for new numbers in a non-pre-released period and in line with this name's real results-day moves (-11.9, +8.5, -4.2, +0.7, -9.8, +4.0). p_up left at 42 and finding sizes unchanged.

Also noted: the baseline's history dates are off by one or two days from the actual RNS dates (e.g. it uses 2025-11-04 against the 2025-11-06 release, 2026-05-07 against 2026-05-06), so its 4.26% median understates the name's results-day scale.
